subject: Post-demo recap: JSON output flow, retry strategy, and evaluation links

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-demo recap: JSON output flow, retry strategy, and evaluation links

Hi Alice —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned with Acme's evaluation goals: 

1) Model fit & benchmarks
- Recommended starting models: Llama 3 16B quantized (fast baseline), Mistral-instruct-7B (cost-efficient), and optionally Llama 2 34B for high-quality transcription of domain prompts.
- I've attached a short benchmark run (link below) with latency/cost numbers from similar structured-output workloads.

2) Structured output (JSON) plan
- We'll validate JSON schema compliance with our structured-output harness using the schema you shared (attached as json-schema-vendor-output.json).
- Suggested initial scope: 500 prompt variants across your two most common forms (order summary, eligibility check).

3) Tool/function calling reliability
- We'll instrument retries at the runtime layer: exponential backoff with jitter, idempotency keys for side-effecting calls, and a two-tier fallback: if tool-call fails after N retries, return a structured error object rather than free text.

4) Eval artifacts we will provide
- Prompt set v1 (attached) + reproducible runner, benchmark links, and a small regression test harness we can run on Dedicated or Private.

Next steps I propose:
- Acme to send the finalized JSON schema and a short sample of 50 real prompts by Friday (6/25).
- Redwood to deliver a draft evaluation run (500 prompts) and suggested model mapping by 6/30.

Attachments: ACME-Sec-Questionnaire.pdf (if you want us to start the security review in parallel), prompt-set-v1.md, json-schema-vendor-output.json

If that timeline works, I’ll schedule a follow-up next Tuesday for results review.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: JSON output flow, retry strategy, and evaluation links

Folks —

I reviewed Alice's returned schema and examples. A couple of pragmatic suggestions for the initial eval run: 

- Model mapping: start with Mistral-instruct-7B for the 80% lightweight path (low-cost, low-latency) and Llama 3 16B-quant for the 20% complex parsing cases. Keep Llama 2 34B as a bench for highest-quality candidates where tokenization issues occur.

- Retry strategy for sync API calls: 3 attempts, base delay 150ms, exponential backoff factor 2, max jitter 100ms. If total elapsed > 1.2s return structured status {"status":"degraded","code":"TOOL_TIMEOUT"} so frontend can render a lightweight fallback. For async/background jobs, we can increase retries and run a compensating job with idempotency keys.

- JSON schema validation: run schema-first validation on model output, then a lightweight semantic check (presence/format of critical fields). We'll log both validation failures and semantic regressions into the eval harness.

- Benchmarks: I kicked off a small warmup run (50 prompts) on a Dedicated test pool. Link: https://redwood-inference-benchmarks.example.com/acme-run-2026-06 (results will be added by EOD).

I'll draft a short runbook with the exact commands for them to run locally if they want to try Private. Laura — can you attach the runbook and the prompt variants we discussed?

Karthik
Director, Solutions Engineering
karthik@redwood.ai
